public_rationale: Zuckerberg did identify AI as Meta's largest investment in March 2023, within two years of the rebranding. The announcements support a change in public strategic emphasis. This assessment does not establish that AI newly overtook metaverse spending or that Meta abandoned the metaverse.
limitations: The result depends on reading 'pivoting' as a change in emphasis.
The investment ranking is management's description, without a defined accounting measure.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Less than two years after renaming itself, Meta is pivoting again from the metaverse to AI as its largest investment.

statement.excerpt: And now, less than two years after the name change, Meta is pivoting again, with Zuckerberg saying that Meta’s “single largest investment is advancing AI and building it into every one of [their] products].”

from_speaker: less than two years after the name change
single largest investment is advancing AI
our_interpretation: Read 'pivoting' as a change in publicly emphasized strategic priorities, not necessarily abandonment of the metaverse.
Test the company's characterization of its largest investment. The statement does not specify an expenditure amount or establish that metaverse spending previously ranked first.
The comparison runs from the rebranding to the post date.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporary announcements establish the rebranding date and an increased strategic emphasis on AI, with Zuckerberg identifying AI as Meta's largest investment before the post.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The attributed investment statement is inaccurate, the timing is wrong, or contemporary announcements do not establish the claimed change in strategic emphasis.
